Describe_your_core_program_s:
Malaika is an African-led grassroots nonprofit that envisions resilient, self-reliant communities
empowered through education, skills, and health programmes.
Malaika’s main goal since its inception in 2007 is to invest in girls’ education but it is also committed
to lifting girls’ communities out of poverty through livelihood, WASH, and agriculture initiatives.
Malaika has impacted the lives of thousands of children and their families in rural Kalebuka, DRC.
Through the Malaika School, a free, accredited institution serving 430 girls, all girls aged 5-19 in
Kalebuka have access to a quality education. The school's innovative curriculum ensures students
are provided with a well-rounded education that includes STEM subjects, French, English, math,
computer science and the arts.
The Malaika Community Center offers health, literacy, and sports programs for over 5,000 youth and
adults in the wider community each year, as well as a vocational training program which offers high quality vocational training for future electricians and mechanics.
Finally, Malaika’s clean water program has built and refurbished 31 wells, providing over 45,000+
people each year with clean water
Organisation_s_mission:
Malaika’s mission is to empower girls and their communities to reach their full potential through
education and local community transformation. We do this by providing free education, clean water,
vocational, agricultural, athletic, and health programs.
Overview:
Malaika was founded to address the lack of educational opportunities for girls in rural DRC. It began as a sponsorship programme for orphaned children and evolved into a holistic education and community development ecosystem.

Core components include:

Free primary and secondary school education (ages ~4–19)

Community centre (literacy, vocational training, health, sports)

Agriculture (school meals)

Water access (32 wells serving ~37,000 people)

The organisation operates a fully subsidised model, covering tuition, meals, transport, and materials.

Describe_your_core_program_s:
1. Teacher Capacity Building and Professional Development

MCT provides high-quality teacher training and professional development for early childhood educators. Through our training programs, teachers gain practical skills in child-centered pedagogy, classroom management, and developmentally appropriate learning practices.

A flagship component of this work is the Community Rooted Early Education (CoRE) Program, which equips teachers with internationally recognized Montessori-based training certified by the Association Montessori Internationale (AMI). The program combines structured coursework, mentorship, and classroom-based practice over a period of approximately ten months to ensure meaningful transformation in teaching practice.

2. Systems Strengthening and Institutional Partnerships

MCT works closely with government institutions, universities, NGOs, and education networks to strengthen the early childhood education ecosystem in Tanzania. We contribute technical expertise, training support, and collaborative learning platforms that help align community-based education initiatives with national education policies and quality standards.

Through strategic partnerships, MCT supports the scaling of quality early learning models within public and community education systems.

3. Community Engagement and Child-Centered Learning Environments

MCT supports schools and communities in creating stimulating, inclusive, and child-centered learning environments that promote holistic development. This includes guidance on classroom setup, learning materials, and practices that nurture children's independence, creativity, social development, and love for learning.

Describe_your_core_program_s:
•	The Sega Girls Secondary School; a boarding school providing quality, holistic education to about 280 girls annually, the majority of whom receive full scholarships. In addition to teaching the national academic curriculum, the school teaches life skills, leadership, environmental stewardess, and entrepreneurship skills.
•	The Continuing Education Scholarship Program; provides scholarships to nearly 300 SEGA School graduates annually so that they can pursue higher education. Scholarships are provided to all qualifying graduates, which enable them to pursue certificates and diplomas, A-Levels (Advanced High School degrees), university degrees, vocational training, internships, and short-term courses. Most of our graduates attend competitive higher education institutions in Tanzania, but a few have attended prestigious universities abroad, including Ashesi University in Ghana, and African Leadership University in Rwanda. 
•	Modern Girls Community Outreach Program; a peer education program in which the recent SEGA graduates mentor girls and young women in their home communities and teach them about life skills, sexual reproductive health, human rights, entrepreneurship, financial literacy, and renewable energy. The program reaches 1800- 2000 girls and young women weekly and annually in 31 communities throughout Tanzania during the critical ages when most are at risk of early pregnancy, early marriage, and dropping out of school. 
•	SEGA Graduates Business Fund: this is a business coaching program that also provides a small revolving loan to SEGA graduates who have started business post school. Those who have decided to focus on business and have taken initiative to start their own business, SEGA aids in providing micro loans and knowledge to help them grow their business well.

The organisation now runs four programmes: a secondary school for girls, a continuing education scholarship programme, a community-based Modern Girl programme, and a graduate business fund. The organisation focuses on providing holistic education to girls from marginalised communities, including academic education, life skills, entrepreneurship, environmental education, and leadership development. Approximately 85 percent of students receive scholarships

Describe_your_core_program_s:
Science Fuse engages children aged mainly 3 to 14 in dynamic STEM learning experiences across classrooms, festivals, orphanages, and hospitals. Through hands-on activities, active experimentation, and real-world problem-solving, we spark curiosity, build scientific literacy, and empower children to see science as part of everyday life. 

Our offerings include: 

STEM Workshops and Science Shows (e.g., Science Tamasha) for short, impactful sessions. 

STEM Clubs that run for several months or a full year, providing sustained engagement. 

Science Festivals that bring together children, parents, teachers, and communities for experiments, live demos, interactive talks, and competitions. 

To ensure lasting impact, we train educators through professional development programs focused on: 

The Science Capital Teaching Approach. 

Integrating Science Inquiry Skills into lessons. 

Using storytelling to make science relatable. 

We also help schools set up STEM Clubs, Science Shows, and STEM-themed events, creating environments where curiosity thrives long-term, and support youth (16+) through fellowships and programs that build science communication and equity-in-STEM skills. 

Beyond direct programs, we produce locally relevant STEM resources such as books, posters, podcasts, and video lessons featuring relatable characters and diverse scientists. Through DIY experiments and culturally rooted storytelling, we help children see themselves in science while connecting them to global innovations. 

Our partnerships often start with short activities and grow into multi-year collaborations, ensuring deep and sustained impact.

Beyond direct interventions, Science Fuse also develops locally relevant STEM resources such as books, posters, podcasts, and video lessons featuring relatable characters and diverse scientists.

Describe_your_core_program_s: Community Childcare Project (CCP): The CCP is our flagship model for upgrading childcare quality in informal and formal settings. We train and mentor childcare providers on safety, early learning, child protection, nutrition, and business management while equipping them with tools and ongoing support. CCP also engages parents through workshops and community campaigns. The model enhances childcare quality, empowers parents, and expands access to affordable early learning environments. Healthy Nutrition Project: This program improves child nutrition by supporting the production of nutritious whole-grain cereals for children 6 months and above. Through CCP-trained providers across Lagos and Ogun States, these cereals reach families who need them most. The initiative addresses malnutrition while creating an additional income stream for childcare providers, strengthening sustainability. Coalition of Childcare Providers of Nigeria (CCPN): CCPN organizes childcare providers into a national platform for professional development, peer learning, and collective advocacy. It gives providers, especially those in informal communities, a unified voice to influence policy, improve standards, and access support. Policy-Relevant Research: NECCS conducts research on childcare quality, parent needs, and women’s economic empowerment. Evidence generated aim to shape policies, informs program design, and supports scalable childcare solutions. Business Champions for ECD: This program mobilizes private-sector leaders to invest in ECD, promote employer-supported childcare, and adopt family-friendly workplace policies, strengthening sustainable financing for childcare.
Organisation_s_mission: To ensure every Nigerian child in the early years has access to affordable, high-quality, nurturing childcare by strengthening childcare systems, empowering parents, engaging communities, and advocating for supportive national policies.

This is delivered through a suite of programmes — Apto Lead, Apto Teach, Apto Coach, Apto Teams, Apto Selfie, Apto Inspire (SEN), and Apto Early Years — each designed to build capacity at multiple levels of the education system. Overview:
Teach Me Well Ghana is a community-driven education organisation focused on improving foundational literacy and numeracy skills in underserved and rural communities in Ghana. It applies the evidence-based Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) methodology, tailoring instruction to learners’ actual learning levels to accelerate progress in literacy and numeracy.

The organisation operates through a combination of in-school support, vacation learning camps, and community engagement activities to ensure that children who are behind achieve measurable gains in foundational skills. Its approach emphasises data-driven instruction, volunteer mobilisation, and partnerships with local education stakeholders.

Organisation_s_vision: Our vision is to ensure that one day, everyone has the essential skills to thrive. Describe_your_core_program_s: Our core programmes globally are delivered through a proven four-stage model designed for maximum scale and systemic impact, all centred around the Skills Builder Universal Framework: 1. Schools & Colleges: We partner directly with schools and colleges (in over 20 countries) to run the Accelerator programme, investing in Skills Leaders and providing comprehensive teacher training and resources to drive rapid, measurable progress in essential skills. 2. Local NGO Partnerships: We collaborate with local Non-Governmental Organisations and training providers globally to embed the Framework into their existing programmes, offering upskilling and quantifying the impact on their beneficiaries. 3. National Lead Partners: We establish long-term partnerships with credible national champions to adapt, translate, and scale the approach across an entire country's ecosystem, building a local provider network. 4. System Strengthening: We engage with governments and education systems (e.g., in Kenya and Uganda) to build the Universal Framework into the national curriculum, teacher training, and school inspection regimes, ensuring sustainable, whole-system change for all learners.

Organisation_s_vision: To foster a Sierra Leone where every child and youth, regardless of background, can access an excellent education and is empowered to act as a catalyst for positive change within their communities and the nation.
Schools_demographics: SLEA works with 10 low-fee, government-assisted and community-founded schools in Bombali District, primarily located in rural and remote communities. These schools serve students from low-income households, often in areas where access to qualified teachers and learning materials is limited. The majority of partner schools are rural, and they charge modest fees rather than being fully free. The organisation currently supports approximately 1,200 students across these schools.
Describe_your_core_program_s: Core Programs The Sierra Leone Educators Association (SLEA) delivers a suite of integrated programs designed to holistically address the educational ecosystem. Our initiatives target students, teachers, schools, and communities to foster sustainable development and empower the next generation of leaders. 1. Literacy for All Program We combat illiteracy through comprehensive, evidence-based initiatives that equip learners of all ages with foundational competencies in reading, writing, and critical comprehension. Our programs are implemented in both school and community settings to ensure nationwide impact. 2. Teacher Empowerment Initiative Recognizing that teachers are the cornerstone of quality education, we provide continuous professional development. Our training modules focus on modern pedagogical techniques, subject-matter mastery, and psychosocial support, fostering a valued, motivated, and highly effective teaching force. 3. Human Rights & Civic Education We are dedicated to weaving the principles of human rights and civic responsibility into the fabric of society. Through targeted engagement with students, youth, teachers, and parents, we build a culture of awareness, respect, and active citizenship. 4. Green Schools & Community Action Program This program transforms schools into vibrant hubs for environmental stewardship. Using a hands-on, practical model, students lead projects in school gardening, reforestation, and community clean-ups, directly linking learning to sustainable development. 5. Youth Skills & Entrepreneurship Development We bridge the gap between education and economic opportunity by providing youth and women with market-relevant skills training. Our curriculum encompasses technical and vocational skills, digital literacy, and essential soft skills to enhance employability and entrepreneurial success. 6. School Health & Well-being Advocacy A healthy learner is a productive learner. We advocate for and educate on public health within schools
Organisation_s_mission: Our mission is to transform education and empower youth in Sierra Leone through strategic partnerships and systemic intervention. We build resilient educational systems, pioneer innovative learning programs, and provide leadership development to equip students, teachers, and communities with the knowledge, skills, and ethical foundation to drive sustainable progress in education and youth empowerment.
Overview:
Sierra Leone Educators Association (SLEA) is a youth-led, nonprofit education support organisation founded in May 2022 and based in Makeni, Bombali District, Sierra Leone 
The organisation works with low-fee community and government-assisted schools in remote areas to improve the quality of education through teacher capacity building, student life skills programming, literacy support, and environmental education initiatives.

Sierra Leone Educators Association (SLEA) partners with schools to deliver comprehensive literacy programs for children and out-of-school youth. By focusing on reading, writing, communication, and practical application skills, they combat illiteracy and unlock potential.

Their initiatives foster a lifelong love for reading and enhance employability, targeting both early childhood development and adult learners to break cycles of poverty and build stronger communities in Sierra Leone.

To achieve this, they improve school infrastructure, distribute learning materials, train & motivate teachers, and implement mentorship programs in our partner schools.

SLEA does not operate schools directly. Instead, it partners with existing schools to strengthen teaching quality, support vulnerable learners, and promote child protection, human rights education, and green school practices. The organisation began working with two schools and has since expanded to ten schools, reaching approximately 1,200 students 

SLEA is registered at the district level with the Ministry of Education (Bombali District), Bombali District Council, Ministry of Social Welfare, and the Bombali District Human Rights Committee 

. It operates through a small youth-led administrative team supported by a five-member board.

The organisation was established in response to the founder’s direct exposure to education inequality and the growing number of children excluded from formal schooling.

The initiative began as a community outreach model delivering literacy and numeracy support through mobile classrooms across villages. However, over time, the organisation identified that this approach was not sustainable, as children would return to under-resourced or misaligned schooling environments. In response, Evolufy transitioned to a structured school-based model in 2023, establishing formal campuses to provide continuity, structure, and long-term support to children.

The organisation is currently led by its founder, who serves as Executive Director, and is supported by a Board of Trustees and a distributed team across Nigeria and internationally.

Describe_your_core_program_s: The Reach to Teach Foundation works with State Governments on strengthening Leaning Outcomes in Government schools at scale by focusing on the twin elements of experiential learning and designing for teacher led interventions. We currently work in four States– Gujarat, Haryana, Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya – focusing on system realignment, scale and sustainability. Our work is based on design-led principles and we work with the Education Department and their functionaries and teachers to consult and design interventions collaboratively. This co-creation has led to ownership by the Department and we train district level functionaries and teachers through a ‘doing and learning’ approach on the use of the material and tools thus collaboratively designed. These people in turn become the State’s feet on street, implementing our design across every school in the State. It is a fully hands on model and has several advantages, The implementation is by the Government system across all Government schools in a State leading to system change at scale. This allows for a small team at our end to drive large-scale improvement. We have Project Management Units embedded in the State Council for Educational Research and Training (SCERT) and a dedicated helpline for continuous support to teachers and other functionaries in the value chain. We have set up communities of practice by creating subject-wise, District- wise WhatsApp groups which are both sounding boards but also a place for teachers and other functionaries to share anxieties, success and good practice. Within 2 to 3 years of working in Arunachal Pradesh, the Board Exam results have improved significantly and the National Assessment Survey, a national Indice measuring competency based learning amongst students has seen the State climb up from being 35 out of 36 States and UTs to being in the 17th position this year.
Organisation_s_mission: We strive to improve education outcomes by making learning joyful, working with governments, partners, parents and communities, with foundational learning skills at the core.
Overview:
Reach to Teach Foundation is an India-based organisation that works with state governments to improve learning outcomes at scale through system strengthening. While the foundation itself was established in 2018 as a Section 8 non-profit organisation in India, the organisation’s work builds on more than two decades of experience.

Previously, programmes were implemented through Reach to Teach UK and Reach to Teach Private Limited in India under a master services agreement with the UK charity. In October 2025, the private entity was formally integrated into Reach to Teach Foundation, and all programmes and staff are now housed within the foundation.

The organisation initially began by working directly with out-of-school children and supporting them to re-enter the formal education system. Over time, the organisation shifted from direct implementation at the school level to working as a technical partner to state governments. Its work now focuses on strengthening education systems so that improvements in learning outcomes can be achieved at scale through government structures.

Reach to Teach currently works with government education systems in four states in India: Gujarat, Haryana, Arunachal Pradesh, and Meghalaya.

Overview:
Guruji Foundation delivers a dual-programme model focused on supporting students from underserved backgrounds through both school-level and higher education interventions. Its school-based programme, the Adolescent Development Programme (ADP), works primarily with students in Grades 5 to 9 in government-aided and low-fee private schools. The programme focuses on building social capital, confidence, and essential life skills that are often missing from traditional education systems.

The ADP is structured around multiple dimensions of development, including psychological strength (such as resilience and emotional intelligence), intellectual skills (including critical and computational thinking), communication (including spoken English), physical development, and an entrepreneurial mindset. Delivery is blended, combining in-school sessions, peer-led learning models (such as student-led coding instruction using Scratch), and online components for areas like spoken English and socio-emotional development.

In parallel, the organisation runs a higher education programme that supports college students through mentorship, financial assistance, and career guidance. Together, these programmes aim to address both access and capability gaps, with a particular emphasis on enabling students to transition successfully from school to higher education and employment by strengthening their confidence, exposure, and readiness.

Interim evaluations regularly assess relevance, sustainability, and outcomes, while learning informs continuous improvement. Beyond long-term development, GRACE actively supports humanitarian response efforts during disasters and emergencies, working in coordination with local communities and partners. Aligned with the national vision of uplifting the most vulnerable populations, GRACE has defined three core program areas for the next five to ten years. Quality Education focuses on inclusive schooling, teacher development, and E-STEAM learning for all children including girls and children with disabilities. Skills Enhancement and Employment promotes digital literacy, entrepreneurship, and workforce readiness for youth and women. Environment and Climate Change advances environmental education, climate resilience, and community-led conservation initiatives.
Organisation_s_mission: GRACE has adopted two core values – social justice and equity and democracy – for its institutional norms and programmatic operations.

In our in depth program where we work directly with students in classrooms, cumulatively we have worked with close to 20,000 students. In this program we see >25% improvement in foundational literacy and numeracy scores of students, 80% student leaders showing improved confidence, communication and problem solving skills. We have also conducted control-treatment studies in this program that have proved the direct correlation of peer learning program to improved student learning and life outcomes. Organisation_s_vision: Our vision is to provide a better prospect for further education for the urban-poor child.
Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work:
Ultimately, KCC's work will raise awareness on the need for deliberate focus on and customized interventions for people who live in the informal poor communities (slums) in Ghana; An estimate of close to 1 million in Accra alone. 
KCC has a direct and positive impact on the educational readiness of young children from urban poor families. By providing a curriculum aligned with the Ghana Education Services and using the "Learn-through-play" methodology, children in the program are well-prepared for the next level of education. This educational foundation is essential for their future academic success.
The KCC model is uniquely designed for the urban poor population and fits their lifestyle and livelihood. The center currently enrolls 100 kids, 55% of them have kayayoo (plural: kayayei) mOther marginalized group of migrant women and girls mostly from the northern regions of Ghana who travel south to work as head porters in large urban markets and 45% are of profiles similar to the kayayoo, including hawkers, and other market workers.intervention supplements the mother's effort in child care, to ensure that the struggle of urban poverty and frequent migration does not adversely affect the child's later education. This population's profile is characterized by sporadic income, living in informal settlements (slums), unplanned trips to see family back home in Other parts of Ghana, religious obligations, and a language barrier. 
 
The program provides a safe space daily for the child to receive care and education to build in them a learning culture that will develop the foundation they need to be school-ready. It increases parental interest and involvement in their child's development and schooling, building a habit of taking their child to school each morning. This will in turn reduce the school drop-out rate among poorer children in the region, and ultimately break the cycle of poverty among their families. Since 2019, KCC has had four graduations for 21 kids all of whom are successfully enrolled in primary school with the first group currently in primary five. The learning development is complimented by a nutrition and health program to lower the incidence of diseases among the children, lowering the child mortality rate among poorer populations. Since inception in 2017, KCC has held four health screening exercises in partnership with volunteer doctors and nurses for over 800 kids of our target population in the Madina area.
Through learning and development assessments, the program has recorded improved psycho-social wellbeing of the child, improved literacy and numeracy, and an increased excitement about going to school. Frequent engagement with the mOther also provided the opportunity to offer breast cancer screening and sensitization, health and nutrition training, and employment and skill development engagements. As a result, there is an increased awareness of child nutrition and child development by mOther, and better tracking and response to the child's health and nutrition.
Other extended projects by the organization is estimated to reach 1000s of kids in partnership with local low-cost private and public early childhood and kindergartens. 
Kaya ChildCare contributes to the social fabric of the community through the center. It promotes a sense of community and shared responsibility for the well-being of the children, fostering positive interactions among parents and caregivers. By providing a safe and enriching environment for Kayayoo children during the day, Kaya ChildCare may indirectly contribute to reducing the prevalence of child labor, as children are engaged in learning and play rather than engaging in potentially hazardous work.
Organisation_s_mission: The mission of Kaya ChildCare is to provide the right conditions for the timely development of the urban poor child in their early years; to ensure they develop their learning, socio-emotional, and executive function skills while their mOther navigate the challenges of urban poverty.
Overview: Kaya Childcare targets low income families, providing quality child-care services to women porters (Kayayoo mothers) working in the streets and markets of Ghana.

Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: Huddle aims to make a meaningful difference in the schools we support by creating engaging, effective learning environments where students can thrive. Organisation_s_mission: At Huddle Education, our mission is to ensure that every child in South Africa, regardless of their circumstances, has access to excellent high school education. We achieve this by blending inspiring teachers, smart technology, engaging content, and joyful learning spaces.

Organisation_s_vision: Antarang envisions a world where every young adult is productively, passionately and positively engaged in a career of their choice and moves their families and communities out of intergenerational poverty.
Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: The Antarang careers model is a curriculum integrated model that runs through  local governments in 25 districts, has trained over 680 state resources to become career facilitators and enabled over 360,000 students transition into education, employment or training pathways in line with their aspirations.    Our program has shown a 86% transition into higher/ vocational education post class 12, compared to a national average of 57%, and over 48% of our alumni are in high wage and emerging sector careers across banking, tech, sustainability, fitness etc. compared to the national metrics that show that only 42% of youth are employed, primarily in the farm sector.   We have expanded our work to reach 26,000 vulnerable youth in the north-east in partnership with the government of Nagaland, and our proven career readiness curriculum has been adopted by Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu and is being delivered through the state to all high school students.
Organisation_s_mission: By 2030,  government schools in India will enable 2.5 million young adults to enter career pathways of their choice, earn incomes that help them lead better quality lives and serve as role models for their peers.
Overview: Working in India, Antarang Foundation is dedicated to bridging the school-to-work transition for socio-economically disadvantaged youth, primarily from government schools in underserved communities. Their flagship initiative is a comprehensive 4-year Career Awareness and Readiness Model, tailored for students aged 14-18 years in grades 9-12. This integrated approach, delivered by trained Career Facilitators equips youth with the skills, knowledge, and networks necessary to navigate their career pathways.  The curriculum combines psychometric assessments, career-specific modules, exposure to industries, network building, and essential employability skills like CV writing. Recognizing the influence of parents and educators on career decisions, Antarang actively engages these stakeholders including government, creating a supportive ecosystem for the youth.

Organisation_s_vision: Africa Dyslexia Organization is a pioneering advocate for multi-sensory learning techniques for literacy, talent development, and equal opportunities for individuals with dyslexia and related learning differences across Africa.
Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: Our work with schools is transforming education across Africa by equipping teachers with inclusive, multi-sensory teaching strategies and ensuring that learners with dyslexia and related learning differences are no longer left behind. Through targeted teacher training, classroom interventions, and awareness campaigns, we are creating learning environments that recognize and support diverse learners.  Key Outcomes:  Empowered Educators: Thousands of teachers have been trained to identify and support students with dyslexia, leading to more inclusive and effective teaching methods in the classroom.  Improved Student Outcomes: Students who were previously struggling due to undiagnosed learning differences are now experiencing academic growth, increased confidence, and a renewed sense of belonging.  Whole-School Awareness: Our programs foster a culture of understanding and empathy across entire school communities, reducing stigma and encouraging peer support.  Policy Influence: Our work has led to collaborative efforts with education ministries, influencing curriculum design and inclusion policies that benefit all learners.  Sustainable Change: We focus on capacity-building by providing ongoing mentorship, resources, and follow-up support to ensure that the impact of our interventions is long-term and embedded in the school system.  By working directly with schools, we are not only improving literacy outcomes but also driving systemic change that ensures every child, regardless of how they learn, has a fair opportunity to succeed.
Organisation_s_mission: Our mission is to unlock the full potential of those with dyslexia and related learning differences by empowering them with multi-sensory learning approaches, fostering talent development, and creating a clear pathway to professional success. We strive to break down barriers in both education and employment, ensuring that dyslexics can thrive in every stage of their personal and professional lives.
Overview: Africa Dyslexia Organisation (ADO) is dedicated to creating inclusive, equitable environments for individuals with dyslexia and related learning differences. Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: Mobile Creches partnered with the Center for Early Childhood Development and Research (CECDR), Jamia Milia Islamia University, New Delhi in 2018, to conduct an impact evaluation across Mobile Creches Demonstration and Tripartite models. The study concluded in 2020 informed about the comparative impact of Mobile Creches models on child, family and community outcomes. 1034 children under 5 years, 87 parents, 148 community members, 77 creche staff from 23 centres across four cities were covered under the study sample. The research collected both qualitative and quantitative data through standardized tools like School Readiness Instrument (SRI) (for 5-6 years old), Early Learning and Development Standards (ELDS) (for 3-5 years old), and Early Childhood Care and Development Scale (ECCD) (for children under 3 years).  The key findings can be summarized as below:  1.	Both models were comparative in quality and no significant differences were observed in median scores of demonstration and tripartite centres.  2.	Demonstration centres are more successful due to experienced and trained staff. NGO run tripartite centres faced problems of attrition. They require more and regular training and monitoring investments for childcare workers.

Overview: Based in Uganda,Young African Refugees for Integral Development (YARID) is a refugee-led organisation  in Uganda, with a mission to empower refugees through holistic, human-centered approaches.  Their education-based programmes include the Bridging Programme, also known as the Ladder to Learning Project, using the Teaching at the Right Level (TARL) methodology. This initiative emerged after observing that many refugee children were placed in grades below their academic level due to language barriers and financial constraints. By pairing Ugandan national teachers with trained refugee educators, the programme enables refugee children to catch up and thrive. A pilot with 32 children showed notable educational gains, leading to further collaborations with TARL Africa, LEGO Foundation, Street Child, and implementation in Kyaka and Akalabei refugee settlements. YARID also supports lower secondary learners through a Team-Based Learning Approach, aligning with Uganda’s new curriculum to promote peer-led learning and integration.

Organisation_s_vision: UMOVEMENT's mission is to eliminate educational and employment poverty traps in throughout Liberia by operating innovation-focused schools and implementing livelihoods programming for young adults. By meeting this mission, we'll achieve our vision of advancing health, education, and development for children and youth through collective action and community engagement-oriented methodologies.
Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: UMOVEMENT's impact has been experienced by thousands of students and their families, hundreds of staff members benefiting from our employment model, as well as in dozens of Liberian communities. We've grown from 40 schools and 9.077 students to 115 schools serving 22,000 students each year; and from 306 staff to 950. As a result of our efforts, we're measurably increasing student learning outcomes in literacy and numeracy, creating safer schools where corporal punishment and bullying abuses are not tolerated, ensuring more girls enroll and stay in school, and establishing lasting bonds with parent-teacher associations to support stronger communities throughout Liberia.
Overview: UMOVEMENT-Liberia programs include Liberia Education Advancement Program (LEAP) -  a public private partnership (PPP) for education that aims to dramatically improve learning outcomes for pre-primary and primary age children; Give to learn (offering scholarships to girls to access secondary education); and livelihood programming initiatives for young adults.

Organisation_s_vision: Our vision is to see vulnerable children and families in Kibera empowered to reach their full potential.
Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: Close to 1000 children in Kibera have been returned to school to complete their primary education.
Organisation_s_mission: Our mission is to provide quality holistic education and support programmes that help relieve poverty, transform lives, and restore hope amongst vulnerable out-of-school children and families in Kibera, Kenya.
Overview: TPT mainly focusses on remediation of out-of-school children, through their low-fee ECD and Primary school - Chemi Chemi ya Tumaini School. Beyond the school, they run a community library supporting the improvement of literacy and learning outcomes in primary school students in Kibera and create a reading culture in the community and a Secondary education programme providing scholarships to attend school, mentorship, life-skills and career counselling.

Organisation_s_vision: Transform Schools believes that every child must realise their full potential in school and life beyond
Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: Our programmes operate in low-income government schools in economically backward districts, tribal areas, and among Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes. Data shows that TL has significantly reduced learning gaps in these schools. Since 2019, government school performance in partner State has improved, reducing the gap with private schools. The pass % gap decreased from 15% in 2018-19 to 1% in 2022-23. Furthermore, 98% of students passed the Class 10 board exams in 2022-23, surpassing the 85% target. Students achieving class-level competencies exceeded targets by 21% to 40%. External evaluations show better Math performance and higher Odia competency levels (28% in 2023-24 and 34% in 2022-23) compared to a 22% average for other interventions. Results from an RCT conducted by J-PAL South Asia show improvements in learning for Class 9 students. Students in the treatment group increased their learning in Math, English, Odia, and Science by 40%(Odia) to 200% (Math) more than the control group, equivalent to up to 1.5 years of additional learning.
Organisation_s_mission: Our mission is improving learning outcomes for secondary-school children in India
Overview: Working in India, Transform Schools is committed to improving learning outcomes for secondary school students in Odisha, West Bengal, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh, with recent expansions to Karnataka and Tripura. At the core of its efforts is the Transform Learning (TL) programme, a 50-hour targeted instruction initiative designed to elevate learning outcomes by focussing on foundational competencies, application, and test preparedness. This scalable model is implemented using a system-level approach incorporating state partners who co-lead and co-fund the programme, with innovative use of data and technology to maximize impact.

Organisation_s_vision: TIDE builds and empowers systems to bring about quality and holistic education of the whole child (education of the head, heart, hands, and soul) for all.
Briefly_describe_the_impact_of_your_work: We have seen a meaningful change and sustainable impact on students learning and teachers pedagogy as measured through various tools including pre- and post-tests, student and teacher surveys, and observational measures.
Organisation_s_mission: We envision access to quality education for all. We envision an education system that propels students to think, respect other people and their perspectives, to learn to collaborate, and to deal with the many 21st century issues. We plan to work on sustainable solutions using a systems-based approach wherein 15 years after the initiation of a project, its need is depleted.  We envision a country with a quality of education and development that brings out the best of our world. In a country like India, the provision of quality education for every child remains a challenge. It is crucial to address the issue of quality education for not just the country but also the rest of an interconnected world. The New Educational Policy and Sustainable Development Goal 4 emphasize the importance of inclusive and equitable quality education and their role in life long learning, shaping holistic human beings, and to counter the various issues and challenges of the 21st century.
Overview: Operating in India, Together in Development & Education (TIDE) Foundation works collaboratively with educators, policymakers, and communities to bring meaningful change to learning environments.A key initiative under development is the Block Education Transformation Initiative, designed to drive systemic reforms in government schools, and holistically transform education at the block level, supporting with Teacher support and Classroom pedagogy, Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) and Socio-emotional learning (SEL).In addition to its government school initiatives, TIDE implements a Life-Skills Programme that reaches 10 low-fee private schools and 30 government schools. All TIDE programs and training modules are openly accessible, encouraging replication and adaptation to maximize their impact.

Organisation_s_vision: We envision a future where every child has equal opportunities to access quality education and thrive by empowering low-cost private schools to become centres of excellence and fostering a transformative educational ecosystem in Ghana.

Overview: Think Education works with low-cost private schools in Northern Ghana in capacity building, mentorship and coaching of school leaders as well as running community of practice sessions to encourage learning and sharing among the low-cost private schools.

As educational outcomes evidence of the Education for life programme activities: If no major effect was perceived yet at the end of year 1 intervention (which was normal since the program was still at its installation stage). We could say that the programme activities have contributed to increase the academic performance of the pupils at our schools. The ED4L programme logic model assumes that the integrated approach used by providing pupils with healthy meals through school canteens, by improving health and hygiene practices both in schools and at home through WASH activities, as well as by improving their learning environment could contribute to the improvement of their capacity to learn. This evidence of sustained pupil outcomes from a pre-primary education intervention was ground-breaking in an African context. We have also built 19 sustainable kindergarten schools, two of which are Centres of Excellence, on campus at two Colleges of Education and a third Centre of Excellence at the University of Education, Winneba.

Rangeet is a mobile app for schools, families and communities (facilitators) to support the overall wellbeing and development of children aged 7-16. Only one device is needed to implement the program, which is used by the facilitator. The app features a play-based Social, Emotional and Ecological Knowledge (SEEK) curriculum, as well as teaching-learning resources and activities, designed around the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. SEEK supports existing curricula and is based on the science of learning and develops the skills and competencies necessary to thrive with the understanding that every child learns differently.    The app enables anyone to teach in any socioeconomic, geographic or cultural context, in-person or remotely, at home, in schools and/or communities, even in conflict zones and refugee camps.
